events.name: Solar storm
events.text: The Sun has thrown out a burst of charged particles. It will reach the craft in a few hours.

choices.label: Switch to safe mode
choices.text: Turn the instruments off for a day until the storm passes.
choices.outcome: The craft slept through the storm. One day of images was missed, but nothing was damaged.

choices.label: Keep working
choices.text: Keep taking images and hope the storm is weak.
choices.outcome: Charged particles damaged the solar cells. They now make 10% less power for the rest of the mission.
choices.outcomeIfLucky: Lucky this time: the storm passed without damage. Next time it might not.

events.sourceNote: Space weather can damage solar cells and electronics; spacecraft often go into safe mode during storms. Chance and damage are game estimates.

events.name: Ground station outage
events.text: Bad weather has knocked out the ground stations for 3 days. Nothing can be sent down.

choices.label: Store data on board
choices.text: Keep imaging and send everything when the stations come back.
choices.outcome: The craft stored its images and sent them down after the outage.
choices.outcomeIfFull: Storage filled up during the outage, so some images were thrown away.

choices.label: Take fewer images
choices.text: Image only half as often for 3 days, so storage doesn't overflow.
choices.outcome: Fewer images were taken, but none were lost.

events.sourceNote: CubeSat 101 section 2.10: the ground station is critical, so plan for it being unavailable. Outage length is a game estimate.

events.name: Radio not responding
events.text: The craft's radio has stopped answering. The flight computer can still try things.

choices.label: Reboot the radio
choices.text: Power-cycle it. Usually works, but there is a small chance it won't come back.
choices.outcome: The reboot failed and the radio never came back. No more data can be sent.
choices.outcomeIfLucky: The reboot worked. The radio was back after 6 hours.

choices.label: Wait and watch
choices.text: Leave it alone for 3 days in case it recovers by itself.
choices.outcome: The radio woke up again after 3 days, but no data could be sent while it was down.

events.sourceNote: Rebooting a stuck part is a common first fix in spacecraft operations. Chances are game estimates.
